_comment: What `claude-loadout setup` installs. The marketplace catalog (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) says where each plugin comes from; this says which ones a new developer gets by default, what each person must supply themselves, and the MCP servers no plugin can carry because they authenticate per developer. The wizard reads this from the marketplace clone Claude Code already makes, so it needs no extra credentials.
name: instruxi

plugins.summary: The enforcer MCP server, the shared Enforcer sign-in, the graph worker's hooks, skill and dispatcher, and the governor. Run /enforcer:login, then /enforcer:setup
Risk gates, subagent model routing and verification, a stop self-check, loop detection. Opt in: it judges your commands and reports with TypeSafe's Jev

env.title: TypeSafe Jev key
env.where: console.typesafe.ai — your own key, never shared

notes: The `enforcer` MCP server comes with the enforcer plugin. Sign in once with /enforcer:login; signing in through /mcp instead covers the tools but not the governor.
The Enforcer API is documented by the MCP server itself: enforcer_api_search and enforcer_api_describe answer from the live spec, so there is no separate doc plugin to fall out of date.

No API keys for people: /enforcer:login is one OAuth sign-in for the enforcer MCP server and the hooks inside enforcer. It grants the graph work loop and plan authoring; deletes and plan sharing stay with a person. Scoped keys (GRAPH_API_KEY / ENFORCER_API_KEY) are for CI and containers only.

enforcer is public. jev-hooks is private: installing it needs access to instruxi-io, because Claude Code clones it with your own git credentials. enforcer-graph, enforcer-files and enforcer-governor are deprecated aliases of enforcer and are not offered.
